findings.title: Sparse route pools reuse the same DewSource in multiple pair slots
findings.evidence: When rest.length is smaller than remaining, floor(i * rest.length / remaining) repeats early source indices. PlaneGeometry(2, .0451, 3, 3), detailScale .5, quality high yields 5 pair entries but only 1 unique frame/source identity; height .0453 yields 14 pairs but only 5 unique identities.
findings.impact: The promised fewer-route fallback stacks several pairs at identical positions, drops valid later routes, and aliases launch caches and diagnostic slot states. Full approved B-body pools do not trigger the issue.
findings.recommendation: Compute count = Math.min(remaining, rest.length), then iterate i < count and index Math.floor(i * rest.length / count). Preserve one source object per pair.
findings.resolution: restCount = min(remaining, rest.length) is now both iteration limit and stride denominator. restCount=0 skips the loop safely; when nonzero, rest.length/restCount >= 1 so selected indices are strictly increasing and in bounds. The new sparse-route regression asserts nontrivial sparse fallback and distinct pair frame/source identities.
